A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StreamingVLM and provide readable methods, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained material can be matched reliably despite pagination changes and two added tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original captioning and VQA evaluations, latency measurements, design ablations, and the temporal stability analysis in Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a non-overlapping training comparison and an attention-sink sensitivity study.

M1.justification: The proposed overlapping-chunk training, interleaved vision/text supervision, streaming KV cache, and contiguous RoPE remain unchanged. The new non-overlapping model and sink configurations are experimental variants, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Training data and evaluated task coverage remain unchanged: sports commentary, Inf-Streams-Eval, LiveCC sports captioning, and the four VQA benchmarks. The additions test training and cache configurations within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 7 adds a model trained on the full SFT dataset with standard non-overlapping chunks as a direct comparator to overlapping training. The comparator sets in the retained experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce non-overlapping training and matched training/evaluation sink sizes of 64, 128, 256, 512, and 1024 tokens. This extends Table 5, whose finite-window variants used 512-token training settings. Existing evaluation protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Table 7 adds a direct same-dataset test of the central overlapping-training strategy, addressing the attribution question left by Table 6's data-addition comparisons. Appendix A.3/Table 8 also tests sink size jointly during training and evaluation. Together these substantially extend the analysis of two key design choices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new wording 'significantly better' is not accompanied by a statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Existing results are retained. Table 7 adds non-overlapping versus overlapping scores, including 62.51 versus 66.18 on Inf-Streams-Eval and 59.20 versus 61.96 on OVOBench; VideoMME instead favors non-overlapping training, 65.50 versus 65.10. Table 8 adds sink configurations, while its 512-token row repeats Table 5's basketball values rather than updating the headline results.

T1.justification: The chunk definitions, cache formulation, positional reasoning, and complexity descriptions are unchanged. The added empirical analyses introduce no mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and headline claims: aligned streaming training/inference, Inf-Streams, real-time operation, and VQA transfer. The new experiments support existing claims rather than redefine their scope.

C2.justification: Section 3.4.3 adds hypotheses that data alone are insufficient and overlap is essential for streaming-cache alignment. Appendix A.3 adds an interpretation involving initial-context retention, diminishing returns, and an efficiency tradeoff, recommending scenario-dependent sink tuning.

D1.justification: v2 specifies that the new control uses the full SFT dataset without overlap and documents paired training/evaluation sink sizes. These are limited additional configuration details; existing implementation, compute, and code/data access disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work discussion are unchanged. The new baseline is an internal ablation, without new citations or revised positioning against earlier research.

P1.justification: v2 adds localized experimental discussion and Appendix A.3, renumbers the retained demo section to A.4, and changes the running header to the ICLR 2026 publication statement. Kelly Peng and the First Intelligence affiliation are removed from the byline. The remaining prose and section sequence are largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 7 and 8 are added, with associated text and page reflow. Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–6 retain their content and overall design; the appendix demo moves onto the new final page.

improvement.justification: Table 7 supplies a previously missing comparison of overlap using the same stated SFT dataset, and Table 8 adds useful sink-sensitivity evidence. These strengthen empirical support modestly. However, Table 7 includes a tie and a VideoMME reversal, and neither addition reports uncertainty; the new language of proof and significant superiority therefore exceeds what the evidence establishes.
